items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: But I do like to use some of the styles that I, that I picked up during the years, like, uh, lots of Bix's influence

ctx.x: Yeah. You wanted to ask what I'm up there. I wanted to ask Armin to, if he could play something that would be representative of what he, what he just described as, uh, uh, uh, playing, uh, a style that, uh, Jolly Roll might be playing in, in, in 1976, if he was still alive. Or something like that. Do you have one in particular that you'd like to do on that?

Yes, John, I do. I think I have a tune, uh, that I would like to, to demonstrate, if you might call it that. Um, Y, that was written in him, uh, written by Jolly in later years. And it was a, a rather pretty little melody. A little something different from his regular tunes that he wrote. Yeah. And, uh, as I discussed, uh, with you off the tape there, John, that, uh, that I feel as though that now, uh, I try to play Jolly Roll. You asked me what, what styles or what has mostly influenced me now. Um, I think that…

That's great. All right. Well, let's, yeah, we can move the mic server. If I can have a, untangle them. They're all tied up together. You look at the tape recorder. Um, and you talk to the tape recorder. Huh? You talk to the tape recorder just like it's a human being. You know, that's funny. Why do you know this is going to be weird? That's okay. I just pitched them down. Oh, it's not like this is a professional recording with good mics and everything on them. We just kind of document it, so I throw the mics. stuff

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: We played together out there and we were together and Bix played the trumpet and it was really a great, great thrill.

ctx.x: I want to get back to Dixon in the mist. How did he play on the piano? Did he play more or less legitimately or did he have unusual things?

Well you know, Dixon's piano playing was really amazing because in listening to Dixon's Bix playing piano, I can never really tie in his trumpet with the piano. I don't know if it ever struck you that way, Dick, but listening to his trumpet, it sounds like it's an entirely different phase than his piano playing. His piano sounds so different that it was rhythmical with really sort of modern chords and yet there was the old time flavor along with it. It's just a hard thing to explain, his piano playing. You know,…
Did you ever hear Brownlee's band? Norman Brownlee?
